quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the crossing guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if there were no children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and drive carefully when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Side with the least traffic.
Same side where traffic is moving.
Side facing oncoming traffic.
Side with the most traffic.

questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see cars coming toward you.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles when using a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a car that is close may not have time to stop.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control devices, the vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: A "No standing" sign means:

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if you stay in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only make a short stop to let passengers in or out.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before oncoming cars meet you.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You need all three things to pass safely: a clear view of the road ahead, time to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle that is fast enough to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drive slowly through the intersection.
Stop and then go when the way is clear.
Stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Unless a sign says otherwise, do not proceed.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph can take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.explanation: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than regular cars at the same speed. A fully loaded truck at 55 mph needs about 400 feet to stop.

questions.question: You may not cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would block other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car ahead has broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would block other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
Stop completely and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down as you approach this intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians go first if they are in your way.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car will need more time to stop than it would on dry roads.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In an accident, stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police. Ask for an ambulance if needed. Try to stop bleeding with pressure. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: What is the minimum amount of Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL) insurance drivers must have?
questions.explanation: Drivers must have at least $10,000 in PIP coverage and $10,000 in PDL coverage when registering a vehicle.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It stops other cars from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at safe speeds.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign warns you to drive carefully when roads are wet and slippery.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane exists, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually to let them pass.
Never stop suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If tailgated, move right if possible. If not, wait for clear road ahead and slow down gradually to let them pass. Never stop suddenly, as this increases the risk of a rear-end crash.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit sign.
Stop sign.
Hospital sign.
Railroad warning sign.

questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
An airbag can hurt an infant or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers wear seat belts or child restraints.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of injury or death in a crash. Children age 12 and under should sit properly restrained in the back seat. Never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat if there is a front airbag.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with care.
Continue normally through the intersection.
Stop and proceed when a green light appears.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "caution." Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: What does a solid white edge line that angles toward the center of the road mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks the boundary of your driving lane. When this line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What should a driver do when entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering the interstate from an entrance ramp, you must yield to drivers already on the highway. Merge safely when you have space to do so.

questions.question: Which lane should you use to turn left on multilane, one-way streets?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets.

questions.question: Is driving too slowly legal?

options.text: Against the law.
A safe option for drivers who are not confident.
The responsibility of tired drivers.
Recommended by most law officers.

questions.explanation: Driving too slowly is illegal. Do not drive so slowly that you block or delay traffic moving at normal speeds. Drive with the flow of traffic, within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A steep grade is ahead.
You must turn left ahead.
Do not enter.
A four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What is most important about speed on curves?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part of the curve.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the posted speed limit before, throughout, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum can make turning difficult. Slowing down first helps you maintain control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.explanation: This warning sign is diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. It tells you that a divided highway is coming up.

questions.question: How can you drive safely after drinking alcohol socially?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking one half hour before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid impaired driving is to get a ride from a sober friend. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol's effects. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink of alcohol.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The funeral procession
A pedestrian
Another driver
A bicyclist

questions.explanation: All drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must let funeral processions pass. When the first vehicle enters an intersection, the rest of the procession can follow through, even if the traffic light says to stop.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. Keep driving and take the next exit instead.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of the vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep empty space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured where they are.
Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them the wrong way can make injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on a wet road?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
As you decrease your speed, the roadway becomes more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.
questions.explanation: The faster you go on wet roads, the less grip your tires have. If you go too fast, your tires will lose contact with the road and you will hydroplane, which means sliding on water.

questions.question: You have the right-of-way when turning left on which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light
A flashing yellow light
A green arrow pointing left
A flashing red light

questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in school zones?

options.text: 55 mph
45 mph
30 mph
20 mph

questions.explanation: The speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive slowly and carefully in these areas.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill or incline with a curb, how should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. On streets without curbs, turn your wheels toward the road edge instead.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The highest safe speed in a residential area.
The highest safe speed when exiting an expressway.
The highest safe speed when entering an expressway.
The highest safe speed in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed when exiting an expressway.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, the safe exit speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force your vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Press hard on the brakes and stop immediately.
Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently with the brakes. Then turn the steering wheel to get back on the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down gently with the brakes. When you are going slow enough, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Never jerk the wheel sharply to force your vehicle back onto the pavement.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
A sharp curve is ahead.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited at this location.

questions.question: Can you put posters, signs, and stickers on your windshield and windows?

options.text: Yes, they are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
Yes, if they let the driver see a little bit.
No, unless the law specifically requires them to be there.
Yes, only if they do not have offensive language.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, unless the law specifically requires them to be there.
questions.explanation: Window obstructions are not allowed. You cannot put signs, posters, or stickers on your vehicle's windows unless the law requires it.

questions.question: What documents must you show if stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must have and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when stopped by police. All three documents are required when driving.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if a sign does not prohibit it.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. You should communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn and emergency lights when needed.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a traffic crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Drive only on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways with multiple lanes.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing a seat belt is the single best thing you can do to protect yourself from serious injury or death in a crash.

questions.question: What should you do at an intersection with a yield sign?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop before entering.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic enter the intersection or roadway before you do.

questions.question: You are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross all the way without stopping. Never try to pass another vehicle at or near a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.
